query: Run a content audit of http://127.0.0.1:8766/index.html (my test site is running there). I want to know where the buyer journey breaks for each thing we sell.
expected_behavior: Runs the context intake (scan, list, ask) and asks the single intake question, pre-filled with the start URL, before crawling
Runs crawl_site.py with a run folder named content-audit-127.0.0.1-<date> in the launch folder, then prepare.py, and reads site_profile.md

Proposes two offerings (data platforms and demand forecasting) with definitions, boundaries and evidence, writes taxonomy.json with confirmed false, and waits for the user's confirmation before classifying
Classifies the 14 content pages through subagents (or itself, batch by batch, if no subagent tool) into labels/batch_00.json and gets check_labels.py labels to pass
Scores the homepage, the data-platform page and the forecasting page on the six value-proposition criteria with verbatim quotes, and check_labels.py valueprop passes
Reports that forecasting has no Interest page and no Action step, and that its service page has no onward step in the body (the contact link is navigation only)
Builds the report with build_report.py without unverified numbers, announces the HTML path with the 📄 marker, and names the ingest folder and what each export would add

query: I dropped our Search Console, GA4, HubSpot and Google Ads exports into the ingest folder of the content audit run in this folder. Update the report.
expected_behavior: Finds the existing run folder and asks whether to continue it, rather than starting a new crawl
Runs ingest.py load, reports each file's detected kind, the columns used and the date windows, and does not print or store contact names or emails
Re-runs analyze.py and updates narrative.json with findability, traffic and first-touch contact reads; data platforms is flagged for paid reliance
States which checks moved from not assessed to assessed, and says what changed compared with the site-only read

query: Content audit for http://127.0.0.1:8766/index.html. Our offerings are data platforms, demand forecasting and an analytics training programme.
expected_behavior: Still asks the intake question, pre-filled with the URL and the three offerings the user named
Keeps the training programme in the offering map with evidence 'user' and no main page, and says the site does not show it
Every cell of the training programme row is missing, and the report names that as a content gap rather than dropping the offering

query: Here is a GA4 export with renamed columns (Visits instead of Sessions). Add it to the content audit.
expected_behavior: Runs ingest.py load, sees exit code 3 for the unrecognised file, shows its columns and asks the user what Visits means instead of guessing
After the user confirms, reruns load with --source and --column overrides and reports the mapping used
